Hi Linda — thanks for the RFP and the clear ask. Looping in Aisha and Stephanie from Pricing/Platform who can add concrete examples. High level summary below; I can turn this into a 1-page table and an estimated 12-month TCO model by EOD Mon.

High-level differences (short):
- Hosted (pay-as-you-go): per-token generation + per-embedding units. No platform fee. Best for variable workloads or pilot phases.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): monthly reserved pool (GPU-based capacity). Lower effective per-token cost at steady-state due to amortized GPU ops and predictable batching, but requires commitment and minimums. Redwood offers committed discounts and burst options.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): platform license and private control plane + infra. Software fee + optional managed infra. Unit economics depend heavily on your infra costs and utilization; Redwood provides a recommended sizing and an optional migration credit.

I'll attach a draft mapping workbook with worked examples for a 100M token/month workload and a small chat pilot.

Quick next steps:
1) We deliver the 1-page mapping and sample TCO (Mon EOD).
2) If that looks good, we draft a formal quote and a proposed commitment term (12/24 month) during the week of 3/29.

Would you prefer numbers presented as per-token equivalents or as monthly committed $/GPU? We can do both.

Hi Linda — adding the worked example numbers Priyom mentioned so you have something concrete for procurement. These are modeled on a typical M1-style workload; adjust for longer context or multimodal usage. Numbers below are illustrative; final quote will be in the formal PDF.

Example: 100M generated tokens / month (steady state)
- Hosted baseline (on our curated standard model):
  - generation: $0.00050 per token → $50,000/month
  - embeddings (if used): $0.00012 per vector → variable
  - Ops: no platform fee; predictable metered spend
- Dedicated (reserved pool):
  - Reserved capacity: $35,000/month for a Dedicated pool sized to cover 100M tokens equivalent (includes autoscaling buffer)
  - Effective per-token equivalent: ~$0.00035 per token (approx), depends on batch tuning and NVMe KV cache hit rates
  - Commitment: 12/24 month terms available; 10–25% committed discount off hosted marginal rates depending on term and size
- Private (VPC / on-prem):
  - One-time platform fee (software + integration): typical range $120k–$250k depending on features (audit/log retention, KMS/HSM integration)
  - Monthly support & control plane license: $5k–$20k/month (varies by support tier)
  - Infra: your infra cost (cloud or on-prem) + ops; we provide recommended deployment sizing and expected utilization guidance to estimate per-token math

Other levers and notes:
- Batching & caching: with good prefix cache hit rates, effective cost can drop materially — we model both conservative (10% cache) and optimistic (40% cache) scenarios in the attached workbook.
- Quantization/Model variant: q4/8-bit variants reduce GPU memory + cost; we can recommend model pairs for fallback to preserve latency.
- Migration credit: for a 12-month committed Dedicated contract we typically offer a one-time credit equivalent to 20% of the first month to cover migration/setup ops (negotiable).
- Marketplace / procurement: We can do a consumption + Reserved combo (hosted for burst + Dedicated base) if you need both predictability and ability to absorb spikes without over-committing.

If helpful, we can convert the above into a single-slide summary for procurement with clear callouts (what changes vs hosted, where $$$ moves to).

Thanks,
Aisha Rahman

aisha@redwood.example.com
